registered: 2026-11-04, before any run with a camera in the SO-101 scene; changing it needs a new ADR.
question: Does re-running a seed with a recording camera reproduce the episode the gate judged without a camera, so that a failed-episode video shows that episode?
risk: The camera-on run differs from the judged one in two ways. (1) A camera prim in the scene makes the Isaac Lab launcher enable cameras (isaaclab/app/sim_launcher.py:644-649), so Kit starts from isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit instead of isaaclab.python.headless.kit. The rendering kit adds replicator, the RTX viewport and hydra_texture, and lacks omnigraph.updateToUsd = false. (2) The worker renders between physics steps: SimulationContext.render() calls physics_manager.pre_render() and may call forward(). (1) is the more likely way physics could change.
code_commit: The first commit after this registration that adds recording (a worker --record option and a task option that adds one fixed external camera). Both arms run at that commit; it is stated in the result.

run.worker: piperobot.adapters.isaaclab.evaluate, one Isaac process per seed (ADR 0033), one worker, cuda:0, task robots/so101/envs/vials_to_rack_task_randomized.json

arms.OFF: the normal evaluation, recording off (no camera prim in the scene)
arms.ON: the same seeds with recording on: one fixed external camera viewing the rack and tubes, 640x480 RGB, one frame every 2 control steps (30 fps, 300 frames over the 600-step horizon), written as JPEG

run.order: OFF for both policies, then ON for both policies, all at code_commit, development seeds only (never the gate's 100000-100099). No gate run or runner job is involved.

pass_criteria: All runs exit 0 (infrastructure retries within the evaluator's own budget are allowed and reported).
For each of the 30 seed and policy pairs, OFF and ON give the same success, the same failure label and the same success_step.
For each of the 30 pairs, OFF and ON give the same trajectory_sha256.
failure_rule: Any other result fails the check. The video design then switches to recording states in the camera-off run and replaying them into a render-only scene, under a new plan and registration. No run is repeated under this file.
predictions_not_criteria: PASS: rendering only reads the stage, and the kit file change does not reach PhysX.

OFF reproduces the earlier development runs on these seeds (outcome and trajectory_sha256): base 18/20 matches the --workers test's dev_S; gc12 3/10 matches the C development run. This shows that recording-off code leaves the judged episode unchanged.
measured_no_threshold: GPU memory peak above idle for one camera-on process (nvidia-smi memory.used every 0.5 s; idle is the median of 30 s before the run), against an OFF process.
Seconds per seed, ON and OFF. The first ON run may pay the cold shader compilation (~184 s on the runner, isaac.md); it is reported separately and not counted as steady state.
JPEG bytes per recorded seed. MP4 size comes from the first real gate run (encoded on a hosted ubuntu job).
Projected extra runner time for 5 recorded seeds.
